answer: Reputation-compounded payout lag. New identities earn at an atlas rate: rewards vest only after N epochs of activity, with the release fraction rising toward full speed as history accumulates. Each epoch also applies a tide multiplier that scales payout to current network age, so fresh sybils contribute work but capture saffron-thin returns. To match one seasoned agent’s yield, an attacker must run many identities through the full vesting schedule, paying compute, uptime, and opportunity cost per identity for epochs before any meaningful payout.
